138843429.title: Sentry\Exception\FatalErrorException: Error: Uncaught PDOException: SQLSTATE[42S22]: Column not found: 1054 Unknown column 'legal_document_id' in 'SELECT' in /var/www/html/vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Database/Connection.php:420

The stack frame is 'Command line code(1)', i.e. php -r, not an HTTP request or scheduled job, and the failing SQL is 'select id, legal_document_id, version_number, content from legal_document_versions limit 20'. legal_document_versions has no legal_document_id column; the real foreign key is document_id (see database/schema/mysql-schema.sql). Someone (owner or agent) inspecting the legal documents tables by hand mistyped the column name; production PHP fatals are reported to Sentry regardless of whether they came from a request or a console one-liner. Flagged sensitive because it matched 'legal'. No code touched and none needed. If it recurs from a non-CLI frame, that WOULD be a real defect and should be re-opened.

141439346.title: Error: Object of class App\Enums\EventPublicationState could not be converted to string
141439346.note: Owner authorised the fix after this was first recorded as needs-owner. EventService::canUpdateImage read the root event's publication_status via Builder::value(), which applies the Eloquent cast, so it received an EventPublicationState enum and the (string) cast on it was a fatal Error — every cover-image change on an event with a publication status set failed. Now normalises the enum to its value; the adjacent getRawOriginal() half was already safe and is untouched. Swept all 20 other publication_status reads in app/: this was the only affected site, the only ->value('publication_status') call, and there are no bare enum-vs-string comparisons — so the fix is complete rather than the first of a sweep. Regression tests cover both arms (published must be editable, pending_review must still be refused) and were confirmed to reproduce the production Error against the old code. Sibling suites run: EventsController, EventMutationSafety, EventLifecycleCompatibility, EventsPublicationTransitionCrossTenant — 64 tests green.

142707378.title: GDPR ALERT: 4 data-subject request(s) pending past 25 days (GDPR Art.12(3) requires a response within 1 month). 4 already exceed the 30-day statutory deadline. These need manual action in the admin GDPR queue — there is no automated processor. Sample: #...
142707378.note: GDPR DSAR backlog alarm, and now a diagnosed defect in the alarm itself. Two separate things. (1) The backlog: same standing owner decision as NEXUS-PHP-4A (2026-08-13) - requests #6/#7/#8 (tenant 5) and #11 (tenant 11) are the owner's own admin test requests, so there is no Article 12(3) clock and nothing to action. (2) The respawn: commit 9ed9a316a (2026-08-13) tried to stop this alarm creating a fresh Sentry group every night by calling setFingerprint(['gdpr_request_overdue']) before Sentry\captureMessage(). That commit IS in the live release d0c34906ab49, and it has not worked - NEXUS-PHP-50 (24 Aug) and NEXUS-PHP-51 (25 Aug) are new groups on consecutive days. Root cause: OverdueGdprRequestCheck::raiseAlert() has TWO Sentry paths, and the fix only covered one. Leg 1 is Log::error($message, $context); production's LOG_STACK includes the 'sentry' log channel (config/logging.php:102), so that log line becomes its own Sentry event carrying NO fingerprint, grouped by message text. The message text embeds each request's age in days ('#6 t5 portability 71d'), which increments nightly, so every night is a new group. Proof from the NEXUS-PHP-51 event: tag logger=production and extra key 'log_context' - both signatures of the sentry-laravel LOG HANDLER, not of the explicit capture, whose context block would be named 'gdpr_requests'. Suggested fix (NOT applied - classified sensitive, needs owner authorisation): keep the ages out of the logged message string and pass them only in $context, or send leg 1 to a log channel that excludes sentry. Then one group whose event count is the age of the breach, as commit 9ed9a316a intended. Regression test should assert the logged message is byte-identical on two runs whose request ages differ.

143208420.title: Error: Call to a member function fetchColumn() on bool
143208420.note: GET /api/v2/admin/identity/audit-log returned 500 for every admin on every tenant, for the whole life of the endpoint. All three read methods in IdentityVerificationEventService called DB::statement(...)->fetchAll()/->fetchColumn(), but DB::statement() returns a bool, not a PDOStatement. Changed the reads to DB::select()/DB::selectOne() (the convention already used across app/Http/Controllers/Api/). The INSERT in log() was always correct and is unchanged, which is why events were recorded but never readable. New regression test tests/Laravel/Feature/Services/IdentityVerificationEventReadPathTest.php runs all three reads against a real database; verified failing with the exact production error before the change and passing after. The pre-existing unit test only covered log() and mocked DB::statement() to return true, so it could never have caught this.

143264165.title: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'toLowerCase')
143264165.note: Enterprise admin page crashed for a real member (tenant 4 Timebank Global, user 655) with TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading toLowerCase). Cause: gdpr_audit_log.entity_type is nullable and GdprService::logAction() deliberately passes null when an account is deleted; both EnterpriseDashboard and GdprAuditLog kept a private token builder typed (value: string) that called .toLowerCase() immediately, so one deleted account took the whole admin page down to the error boundary while the API returned a clean 200. Fix was already committed to main on 2026-08-27 as 28948ed1f - a shared null-safe translationToken() in react-frontend/src/admin/modules/enterprise/gdprAuditTranslations.ts falling back to the existing 'unknown' key. NOT authored by this triage run. Verified tonight by running the covering suites (gdprAuditTranslations.test.ts + EnterpriseDashboard.test.tsx, 31 tests, all pass). Still awaiting deploy: live release is 489c627e13b9, built 2026-08-26, before the fix landed.
